summary: BBN announces that IMP number 5 will go off the network on the morning of Saturday March 4, 1972 for a move to a new location, and that a new host called BBN-1D will later join for Network Control Center functions.

plainLanguage.summary: BBN announced that IMP 5 would be taken off the network so staff could move it. The notice also described a new BBN computer planned for Network Control Center work.

questions: when was bbn imp 5 scheduled to move
subtitle: A notice about moving BBN's IMP 5 and adding a host

tldr.problem: BBN needed to move its IMP 5 to another location in its facilities.
tldr.mechanism: The notice schedules the interruption for Saturday morning and says the Network Control Center telephone and operators will remain available.
tldr.outcome: A BBN PDP-1D was also expected to join the network soon afterward for additional Network Control Center functions.

today: RFC 301 is an operational notice dated February 1972. Its text records the planned move of BBN IMP 5 and the planned connection of a BBN host.

sections.title: Moving IMP 5
sections.content:
BBN planned to take IMP 5 off the network at 0800 EST on Saturday, March 4, 1972, so the equipment could be moved to a new location within its facilities. The notice says the Network Control Center telephone and operators would be available as usual during the move.

BBN hoped to reconnect the IMP by early Saturday afternoon, while noting that delays to the wideband lines could extend the outage.
sections.plainLanguage: BBN planned to disconnect IMP 5 while moving it. The Network Control Center would still answer calls during the work.

sections.title: Why the Work Was Scheduled Then
sections.content: The move was planned for Saturday morning to reduce its impact on other network sites if the work or line recovery took longer than expected. The notice expected other sites to operate normally during the period, while IMP 5 was out of service.
sections.plainLanguage: BBN chose a Saturday morning so a longer-than-planned outage would affect fewer network activities.

sections.title: A New BBN Host
sections.content: Shortly after the move, BBN planned to connect a PDP-1D host for additional Network Control Center functions. BBN preferred the host name BBN-1D and assigned it network address 197. The notice says it would not be a server site.
sections.plainLanguage: BBN also planned to connect a PDP-1D called BBN-1D for control-center work. The notice says this computer would not provide server services.
